newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran leader says no back down under U.S. pressure.
newsitem.headline: Iran leader says no back down under U.S. pressure.

text.p: Iranian supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei vowed on Friday that Iran would resist U.S. or other foreign pressure against the Islamic republic.

"If America and all world powers intend to pressure us, this nation wil not back down from its positions. This nation prefers to resist and struggle to bring that united front down to their knees," Khamenei told a mass prayer gathering at Tehran University.

"We shall not surrender...No matter how much pressure -- economic, political, especially military -- is increased on this nation, its (Iran's) determination and will to resist will increase," he said.

The United States severed diplomatic ties with Iran in 1980. In 1995 U.S. President Bill Clinton imposed unilateral but sweeping trade and investment sanctions against Tehran as part of a "dual containment" policy against Iran and Iraq.

Tensions between the two countries have been sharpened in recent months following hints by U.S. officials and Gulf Arab sources of an Iranian connection to a bombing in Saudi Arabia in June that killed 19 U.S. airmen.
Tehran has repeatedly denied any role in the attack.

Washington accuses Tehran of sponsoring terrorism and seeking to develop nuclear arms. Iran denies the charges and says the United States seeks to destroy its government for challenging U.S. hegemony in the Middle East.
